 Soorasamharam 2026 falls on November 15. Check Skanda Sashti fasting dates, Shasti Tithi timings, rituals and the significance of Lord Murugan’s victory over Surapadman.

 Soorasamharam 2026 Date: Skanda Sashti fasting, tithi timings and significance of lord Murugan's victory Soorasamharam 2026 falls on Sunday, November 15.
 Festival marks Lord Murugan's victory over Surapadman.
 Devotees observe six days of fasting and special prayers.

 Soorasamharam 2026 will be observed on Sunday, November 15, marking one of the most significant days dedicated to Lord Murugan, the Hindu deity of courage, wisdom and victory. Also known as Skanda Sashti or Kanda Sashti, the festival commemorates Lord Murugan’s legendary victory over the demon Surapadman, symbolising the triumph of good over evil.
 The occasion holds special significance for Tamil Hindu devotees, who observe a six-day period of fasting and worship during Kanda Sashti. The celebrations culminate on Soorasamharam, the final and most important day of the festival.
 Devotees visit Murugan temples, participate in special prayers and observe religious rituals to seek the deity’s blessings. The celebrations at Thiruchendur Murugan Temple in Tamil Nadu are particularly renowned, drawing large numbers of devotees every year.
 Soorasamharam 2026 Date and Shasti Tithi Timings 
 According to the New Delhi Panchang, the Shasti Tithi timings for Soorasamharam 2026 are:
 Shasti Tithi Begins: 11:23 PM on November 14, 2026
 Shasti Tithi Ends: 2:00 AM on November 16, 2026
 Soorasamharam: Sunday, November 15, 2026
 Kanda Shasti Vratam Begins: Tuesday, November 10, 2026
 Subrahmanya Shasti: Tuesday, December 15, 2026
 The timings are based on New Delhi local time. Panchang calculations may vary by location, and devotees are advised to check their local timings before observing the rituals.
 What is Soorasamharam? Significance of Skanda Sashti 
 Soorasamharam is the concluding day of the six-day Kanda Sashti festival dedicated to Lord Murugan. According to Hindu mythology, Lord Murugan defeated the demon Surapadman after a fierce battle, restoring peace and protecting the celestial beings.
 The festival is observed to mark this victory and represents the triumph of righteousness over evil. Devotees believe that worshipping Lord Murugan during Skanda Sashti helps them seek courage, spiritual strength and divine blessings.
 Skanda Sashti is observed during the sixth lunar day, or Shasti Tithi, of the waxing phase of the moon in the Tamil month of Karthigai. The festival is particularly important among Tamil Hindus, although devotees of Lord Murugan observe it in different parts of India and abroad.
 Kanda Sashti Vratam 2026: Six days of fasting and worship 
 Kanda Sashti Vratam begins on November 10, 2026, and continues for six days, culminating in Soorasamharam on November 15. During this period, devotees observe fasting, offer prayers to Lord Murugan and participate in temple rituals. The nature of the fast varies according to individual beliefs, family traditions and temple practices. Some devotees observe strict fasting, while others follow a more moderate dietary routine.
 The six-day observance is considered an important period of devotion and spiritual discipline. Many devotees recite Murugan prayers, including the Kanda Sashti Kavasam, and attend special worship ceremonies at temples. The final day, Soorasamharam, holds particular importance as it commemorates the defeat of Surapadman.
 Soorasamharam celebrations at Thiruchendur Murugan Temple 
 The Soorasamharam celebrations at Thiruchendur Murugan Temple in Tamil Nadu are among the most prominent Kanda Sashti observances. The temple's six-day festival begins with the start of Kanda Sashti Vratam and culminates in the ceremonial enactment of Lord Murugan’s victory over Surapadman. The ritual, known as Soorasamharam, is witnessed by large gatherings of devotees.
 The celebrations continue with Thiru Kalyanam, the divine wedding ceremony of Lord Murugan, observed on the day after Soorasamharam. For devotees, the festival is not only a religious occasion but also a time to reaffirm faith, seek blessings and reflect on the spiritual message of overcoming negativity through devotion and righteousness.
 Soorasamharam 2026: Religious importance 
 Soorasamharam is regarded as a powerful occasion for Lord Murugan’s devotees. The festival’s central message is that courage, wisdom and righteousness can overcome evil and adversity.
 Through fasting, prayers and temple rituals, devotees seek the blessings of Lord Murugan for peace, prosperity and spiritual well-being. The observance also reflects the enduring importance of Tamil religious traditions and the deep devotion associated with the deity.
